# ontology isolation review 3 (follow-ups: G1 and build review 4 trigger assertion, `43f581c..fb30db2`)

Reviewer: `isolation-reviewer` (opus), 2026-11-15. Read-only; saved by the lead.

**Verdict: APPROVED.** No way for one client to reach another's data through this diff.

1. Naming or probing a group bound only in B: closed. `backend/src/shifde/ontology/service.py:708` accepts a group subject only if it is in `authz.bound_groups(session)`; a group bound only in B and a random id both raise the same `ValidationFailed("no such group")` (same 422, same body), for a client user and for a platform administrator in A. The old `get_group` path leaked: `platform_admin_all` on `groups` reads every row, so an administrator acting in A could name, and so confirm, a group bound only in B. Timing out of scope.
2. `authz.bound_groups` (`backend/src/shifde/authz/repository.py:476`) calls the definer `shifde_bound_groups()` (`identity_0005_platform_groups.py:58`): rows only when `current_tenant_id() IS NOT NULL`, only groups with a `role_bindings` row in the current client; no administrator bypass; id and name only; `search_path` pinned; not redefined later.
3. Other ontology paths agree: `update_policy` (`service.py:776`) checks the policy belongs to this ontology in this client, then the same `_validate_policy`; read-back returns only the stored `subject_id`; at query time `_subjects` (`service.py:151`) -> `authz.subject_ids_covering` -> `shifde_active_group_ids` (`authz/repository.py:164`) requires a binding in the current client, so a policy naming a B-only group matches nobody. No `get_group` or direct `shifde.groups` read remains in `backend/src/shifde/ontology`.
4. Tests not vacuous: `tests/ontology/test_service.py:276` `test_a_group_policy_names_only_a_group_bound_in_the_clients_own_context` fails without the fix in both variants (client user: A's own group refused; platform admin: B's group accepted) and checks the two refusals are identical. `test_model_refs.py:313` (trigger re-enabled after `build_0002`) has no isolation effect. Run at fb30db2: `pytest tests/ontology/test_service.py -k group -n 4`: 4 passed.
5. Info: policies created before the fix by an administrator in a client could name a B-only group; they grant nothing (item 3) and expose only a caller-supplied id. Optional one-off owner query to list and remove `ontology_access_policies` rows with `subject_type='group'` and no `role_bindings` row in the same tenant (no deployed database exists yet, so nothing to clean).
6. Info: no route added; the 422 flows through the existing policy `POST`/`PUT` routes (`ontology/api.py:53`, `:58`).
